source_of_truth: Read by hand from src/components/panel/InfoPanel.tsx (a React function component in a Next.js App Router app, parsed by ui-audit's TypeScript/JSX path). Two independent, provable defects. (1) The <div onMouseEnter={preview}> at line 10 reacts to the pointer (mouseenter) but the file has no onFocus/onFocusIn handler anywhere, so keyboard users never get the preview behaviour: mouse-only-handler, which ui-audit emits at review/heuristic level. (2) The native <dialog> at line 12 carries no aria-label and no aria-labelledby attribute (open is a boolean state, not a name), so a screen reader announces an unnamed dialog: dialog-without-name, provable from the markup (static/confirmed). The two <button>s both have visible text and must not be flagged. Truth derived from the source only; the tool was not consulted while writing it.
provenance: blind generalization: truth derived from source without consulting tool output

expected.rationale: the <div> has onMouseEnter and there is no onFocus/onFocusIn handler in the component; hover behaviour is unreachable by keyboard. ui-audit emits this rule at review (heuristic) level by design, so heuristic is the strongest honest level.
a native <dialog> with no aria-label and no aria-labelledby is an unnamed dialog, provable from the markup; ui-audit reports it at static/confirmed level.

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: both <button>s have visible text content (Details, Close), so each has an accessible name; flagging either would be a false positive.
